# documents

Views, sheets, schedules, tags, notes, dimensions and the rest of a drawing set.

Every example below is a complete script that passes the kit's checks; the kit's tests run each one.

- [`documents.sheet`](#documentssheet): A new sheet (number, name, title block, optional `discipline`, `group`, and `sortOrder` for Views & Sheets discipline grouping/ordering); returns its id.
- [`documents.setSheet`](#documentssetsheet): Changes a sheet's number, name, title block, fields, or sidebar `discipline` / `group` / `sortOrder` metadata.
- [`documents.planView`](#documentsplanview): A floor plan of one level (for a discipline, scale, Revit-standard `viewTopRef`: "level_above" | "associated_level" | "unlimited", `viewTop`/`cutHeight`/`viewBottom`, `browserGroup`, `sortOrder`, detailLevel, symbolScale, showLineCodes, `offsetStackedRuns`, `showReferenceDisciplines`, and per-category/service overrides including singleLineBelow); returns the view's id.
- [`documents.setView`](#documentssetview): Changes a view's `viewTopRef` ("level_above" | "associated_level" | "unlimited"), `viewTop`/`cutHeight`/`viewBottom`, `browserGroup`, `sortOrder`, detail level (coarse/medium/fine), visual style, annotative `symbolScale` (0.5–3.0), inline service codes, `offsetStackedRuns`, `showReferenceDisciplines`, scale, discipline, or per-category/service graphics overrides (including singleLineBelow).
- [`documents.viewTemplate`](#documentsviewtemplate): Creates or updates a reusable first-class view template (`kind: "view_template"`) locking any combination of `view_range`, `category_overrides`, `detail_level`, `visual_style`, `discipline`, `annotations`, and pack-owned `pack_props` (such as `circuitGraphics`).
- [`documents.applyViewTemplate`](#documentsapplyviewtemplate): Binds a view template (by id or name) live to one or many views, or passes `null` to detach the template while keeping the view editable.
- [`documents.viewTemplates`](#documentsviewtemplates): Lists all active view templates in the model with their locks, applicable view types, library source id, and bound view ids.
- [`documents.viewSettings`](#documentsviewsettings): Inspects a view's effective settings (resolved through any bound `view_template`, returning `viewTemplateId`, `viewTemplateName`, `lockedGroups`, effective view range low/high mm & auto top description, browserGroup, sortOrder, and categoryOverrides).
- [`documents.ceilingView`](#documentsceilingview): A reflected ceiling plan of one level; returns the view's id.
- [`documents.sectionView`](#documentssectionview): A vertical building section cut from `from` to `to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); supports `referencingView`, `showInDisciplines` (e.g. `["architecture"]` to filter which discipline plans print the section marker), `categoryOverrides` (e.g. `{ pipe: { detailLevel: "fine" } }`), `headExt`/`tailExt`, `splitGap`, explicit `crop`, and `levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm`.
- [`documents.elevationView`](#documentselevationview): An interior or exterior elevation looking from `from..to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); supports `referencingView`, `showInDisciplines`, and `categoryOverrides`.
- [`documents.view3d`](#documentsview3d): A saved 3D view with its 3D crop box, live projection (`perspective` or `orthographic`), and camera (`lookFrom` corner/side preset or explicit `eye`/`target`, vertical lens angle `fovDeg` in 5–120°, and `orthoHeight`).
- [`documents.setCamera3d`](#documentssetcamera3d): Updates a saved 3D view's camera (`fovDeg` 5–120°, `lookFrom`, `eye`/`target`, `orthoHeight`, or `projection`), preserving any unspecified fields from its current camera.
- [`documents.enlargedPlan`](#documentsenlargedplan): A Revit-style enlarged plan in one step: creates a cropped plan view on the same level at enlarged scale (default 1/4" or 1/2" = 1'-0") with either a rectangular box (`from`..`to`) OR a custom closed L-shape / P-line `polygon` crop, AND places a live parametric callout bubble on the parent plan whose detail#/sheet# head auto-updates when the enlarged plan moves sheets.
- [`documents.callout`](#documentscallout): Places a live parametric callout box or custom L-shape / P-line `polygon` + split head bubble on a view referencing any existing enlarged plan, 2D detail, section, or elevation view.
- [`documents.setCalloutBoundary`](#documentssetcalloutboundary): Reshapes an existing enlarged callout's extents — either to a new rectangle (`from`/`to`) or to a custom closed L-shape / P-line `polygon` (>= 3 corners) — and atomically syncs the referenced enlarged plan view's crop box and polygonal `cropPolygon` in lockstep (Revit behavior).
- [`documents.setCrop`](#documentssetcrop): Sets a view's rectangular crop box (`from`/`to`) or custom closed polygonal `cropPolygon` (L-shape / P-line, or `null` to reset back to a rectangle), toggles cropView/showCropBox, or adjusts section/elevation far clip depth, level datum extensions (`levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm`), and section mark `headExt`/`tailExt`/`splitGap`.
- [`documents.duplicateView`](#documentsduplicateview): A copy of a view (another discipline's plan of the same level); returns the new id.
- [`documents.place`](#documentsplace): Puts a view (a plan, a schedule, a detail) on a sheet at a point (its centre, from the sheet's lower-left corner), with optional scale and viewport title/north-arrow offsets; returns the viewport's id.
- [`documents.setViewportTitle`](#documentssetviewporttitle): Moves a placed viewport's title block on its sheet (`offset`) and/or changes the horizontal title underline length (`ruleLength`, or `null` to reset).
- [`documents.setViewportNorthArrow`](#documentssetviewportnortharrow): Shows, hides, or repositions a placed viewport's north arrow on its sheet (`offset`, or `null` to reset to the default corner).
- [`documents.editSchedule`](#documentseditschedule): Edits a list schedule view in one undo step: add, move, remove or rename columns, filter, sort, group, totals (an equipment schedule's sort, a fixture schedule's DFU total).
- [`documents.schedule`](#documentsschedule): A schedule view; returns its id.
- [`documents.tag`](#documentstag): A tag on one element in a plan view (its mark, size or the right text for its kind), with a leader; returns the tag's id.
- [`documents.moveTag`](#documentsmovetag): Moves an existing tag in a plan view to a clear position (and optionally toggles its leader).
- [`documents.planLabels`](#documentsplanlabels): Returns every rendered text label on a plan view (paper mm coordinates and bounding boxes) plus any overlapping pairs, so scripts can verify legibility and move colliding tags.
- [`documents.dimension`](#documentsdimension): A dimension between two points in a view, tied to elements with refs so it follows them; returns its id.
- [`documents.tagStyle`](#documentstagstyle): A new tag style: field lines, box, orientation, what it applies to, and an arrow along the run (`arrow: "down_slope"` points downhill on the view's paper, `"up_slope"` uphill; level pipe shows none); returns its id.
- [`documents.setTagStyle`](#documentssettagstyle): Changes a tag style's look: lines, box, orientation, applies-to, mask, textStyleId or its arrow (`arrow: "none"` removes it).
- [`documents.textStyle`](#documentstextstyle): Creates a model-wide Text Type (font family, paper cap height, bold/italic/uppercase, opaque or transparent background mask, default drawing roles) so part marks, circuit labels, tags, dimensions and room labels stay unified and readable over crossing lines.
- [`documents.setTextStyle`](#documentssettextstyle): Updates an existing model-wide Text Type (size, font family, bold/italic/uppercase, opaque background mask, color, or default drawing roles).
- [`documents.deleteTextStyle`](#documentsdeletetextstyle): Deletes a model-wide Text Type by id.
- [`documents.flipWireArc`](#documentsflipwirearc): Flips (or explicitly sets) which side an automatic circuit or switch-leg arc bows toward on a plan view.
- [`documents.setCircuitGraphics`](#documentssetcircuitgraphics): Sets a plan view's circuit and switch-leg drawing style (`showCircuits: false` makes a dedicated controls schematic plan), home runs, switch-leg letters, and ANSI/NECA 100 wire hash marks (`home_runs`, `home_runs_and_switch_legs`, or `all_runs`) while keeping existing wire waypoints and home-run offsets intact.
- [`documents.setSwitchLegLabelOffset`](#documentssetswitchleglabeloffset): Repositions (or resets with `null`) one lowercase switch-leg letter (`"a"`, `"b"`) relative to its device anchor on a plan view.
- [`documents.setMwbcGroup`](#documentssetmwbcgroup): Groups (or splits with `null`) branch circuits on the same panel into a shared-neutral Multi-Wire Branch Circuit (MWBC, NEC 210.4) drawn as one multi-arrowhead combined home run with shared neutral hash marks.
- [`documents.setWirePath`](#documentssetwirepath): Pins one or more spline/orthogonal control vertices on a circuit or switch-leg wire span (`hintKey` is the link id or `"switch:<leg>"`). 1 point draws a smooth arc, 2+ points draw a Catmull-Rom spline, and `null` resets to automatic routing.
- [`documents.setHomeRun`](#documentssethomerun): Aims, resizes, curves, re-attaches, or moves the label of a circuit's home run arrow using offsets relative to its host device so the home run still follows when the device moves.
- [`documents.keynote`](#documentskeynote): Gives elements a keynote by its key ("P1", "M3"); a keynote tag on a view prints the key and the sheet's keynote list (Sheets › Live table › Keynote list) gives its words from the keynote tables in force.
- [`documents.listStandardNoteSets`](#documentsliststandardnotesets): Lists reusable discipline general-notes and specification sets (electrical-general, electrical-demolition, mechanical-general, plumbing-general, fire-protection-general, architectural-general, structural-steel-concrete) so scripts pull standard notes instead of regenerating boilerplate.
- [`documents.placeStandardNotes`](#documentsplacestandardnotes): Places a formatted, numbered standard general-notes block from the reusable library onto a sheet or view, with optional custom title, extra project-specific notes, or excluded starter note numbers.
- [`documents.renderSheet`](#documentsrendersheet): Queues a PNG image of one sheet (by id or sheet number) to be rasterized by the host and returned directly in bim_run_script's answer.
- [`documents.renderView`](#documentsrenderview): Queues a PNG image of one view (by id or exact name) to be rasterized by the host and returned directly in bim_run_script's answer.
- [`documents.scheduleRows`](#documentsschedulerows): A schedule's rows as numbers and words, on the model as the script has it so far: cells by column id (quantities in SI), grand totals, the row count.
- [`documents.scheduleFields`](#documentsschedulefields): What a schedule can list and show: every class (no argument), or each named class's fields (path, label, type, unit, how it totals) and relationships for aggregate columns.
- [`documents.autoTag`](#documentsautotag): Tag every untagged element of `categories` (`duct`, `pipe`, `air_terminal`, `equipment`, `fixture`, `part`, `room`, `space`, `opening`) in a view as movable `DrawingItem` tags placed clear of linework and other tags.
- [`documents.autoDimension`](#documentsautodimension): Dimensions runs, walls or grid lines in a plan or section as one edit: each (one dimension along every element) or chain (one string across them).
- [`documents.packSheet`](#documentspacksheet): Arranges a sheet's viewports in its drawing area (the editor's Arrange): packed or a grid, optionally shrinking views to a standard scale that fits, as one edit.
- [`documents.diagramKinds`](#documentsdiagramkinds): Lists every live diagram kind registered by active packs (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, …) with its label.
- [`documents.diagram`](#documentsdiagram): Creates a live diagram view derived from the model by any active pack (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"air_schematic"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, `"plumbing_isometric"`, …; `documents.diagramKinds(ctx)` lists all available kinds).
- [`documents.oneLine`](#documentsoneline): A one-line, riser, or pack-contributed live diagram in a new drafting view: drawn from a distribution you describe (diagram), or live from the model (live: "one_line", "electrical_riser", "controls_diagram", "plumbing_riser"…).
- [`documents.detailLibrary`](#documentsdetaillibrary): The 2D detail library: components (id, name, category, default size in mm, whether it stretches), hatch and line patterns, line styles and weights.
- [`documents.formKinds`](#documentsformkinds): The form schedule kinds the model's add-ons offer (panel, switchboard, feeder, connection_types, equipment_connections, lighting_controls…) and whether each is the schedule of one element.
- [`documents.formSchedule`](#documentsformschedule): A form schedule view (panel, switchboard, feeder, lighting_controls…) with the add-on's built-in form, filled live from the model; rules (a load read's rules.id) prints code demand factors.
- [`documents.detailView`](#documentsdetailview): Creates a 2D CAD drafting detail view (default scale 16 = 3/4" = 1'-0").

## documents.sheet

A new sheet (number, name, title block, optional `discipline`, `group`, and `sortOrder` for Views & Sheets discipline grouping/ordering); returns its id.

```ts
sheet(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { number: string; name: string; titleBlock?: TitleBlock; fields?: Record<string, string>; discipline?: string; group?: string; sortOrder?: number; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: sheet, drawing, title block, sheets, sheet group, sheet discipline, sort order

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Mechanical plan, Level 1", discipline: "mechanical", group: "Mechanical", sortOrder: 401 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setSheet

```ts

```

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

## documents.viewTemplate

Creates or updates a reusable first-class view template (`kind: "view_template"`) locking any combination of `view_range`, `category_overrides`, `detail_level`, `visual_style`, `discipline`, `annotations`, and pack-owned `pack_props` (such as `circuitGraphics`).

```ts
viewTemplate(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: ViewTemplateSpec): string
```

Topics: view template, template, view range, level above, category overrides, standard, firm library, pack props

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const tpl = documents.viewTemplate(ctx, { name: "Mech — HVAC Plan", viewTypes: ["floor_plan"], locks: ["view_range", "discipline"], discipline: "mechanical", viewTopRef: "level_above", cutHeight: units.ft(4) });

  },
});
```

## documents.applyViewTemplate

Binds a view template (by id or name) live to one or many views, or passes `null` to detach the template while keeping the view editable.

```ts
applyViewTemplate(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string | readonly string[], templateRef: string | null): void
```

Topics: view template, apply template, detach template, view

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const tpl = documents.viewTemplate(ctx, { name: "Elec Power", locks: ["discipline", "annotations"], discipline: "electrical", hideDeviceMarks: true });
    const p1 = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "L1 Power" });
    documents.applyViewTemplate(ctx, p1, tpl);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.sectionView

A vertical building section cut from `from` to `to` (direction +1 left / -1 right, depth default 20 ft); supports `referencingView`, `showInDisciplines` (e.g. `["architecture"]` to filter which discipline plans print the section marker), `categoryOverrides` (e.g. `{ pipe: { detailLevel: "fine" } }`), `headExt`/`tailExt`, `splitGap`, explicit `crop`, and `levelLeftExtMm`/`levelRightExtMm`. Returns the view's id.

```ts
sectionView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: VerticalViewSpec): string
```

Topics: view, section, section cut, building section, section marker, split gap, level lines, discipline filter

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const sec = documents.sectionView(ctx, { name: "Building Section A-A", from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(10) }, to: { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(10) }, direction: 1, depth: units.ft(15), scale: 48, splitGap: true, showInDisciplines: ["architecture"] });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-301", name: "Sections" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, sec, { x: units.mm(400), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setCamera3d

Updates a saved 3D view's camera (`fovDeg` 5–120°, `lookFrom`, `eye`/`target`, `orthoHeight`, or `projection`), preserving any unspecified fields from its current camera.

```ts
setCamera3d(ctx: ScriptContext, view: string, camera: Camera3dSpec): void
```

Topics: view, 3d view, camera, field of view, fov, lens, perspective, orthographic

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const v = documents.view3d(ctx, { name: "Entry 3D", lookFrom: "south_west", projection: "perspective" });
    documents.setCamera3d(ctx, v, { fovDeg: 65 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.enlargedPlan

A Revit-style enlarged plan in one step: creates a cropped plan view on the same level at enlarged scale (default 1/4" or 1/2" = 1'-0") with either a rectangular box (`from`..`to`) OR a custom closed L-shape / P-line `polygon` crop, AND places a live parametric callout bubble on the parent plan whose detail#/sheet# head auto-updates when the enlarged plan moves sheets. Returns `{ viewId, calloutId }`.

```ts
enlargedPlan(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: EnlargedPlanSpec): { viewId: string; calloutId: string }
```

Topics: view, enlarged plan, callout, callout bubble, plan callout, detail callout, polygon, p-line, l-shape, crop polygon

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const { viewId } = documents.enlargedPlan(ctx, {
      parent: plan,
      name: "Enlarged Wet Core",
      polygon: [
        { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) },
        { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) },
        { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(6) },
        { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(6) },
        { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(12) },
        { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(12) },
      ],
      scale: 24,
    });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "P-401", name: "Enlarged Plumbing Plans" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, viewId, { x: units.mm(300), y: units.mm(300) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.callout

Places a live parametric callout box or custom L-shape / P-line `polygon` + split head bubble on a view referencing any existing enlarged plan, 2D detail, section, or elevation view. The head reads the target's live detail#/sheet# automatically; returns the callout's id.

```ts
callout(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: CalloutRefSpec): string
```

Topics: callout, callout bubble, view reference, enlarged plan, detail reference, polygon, p-line

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const detail = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Enlarged Core", scale: 24, crop: { from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) } } });
    documents.callout(ctx, { view: plan, target: detail, from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) }, label: "EEP" });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.setCalloutBoundary

Reshapes an existing enlarged callout's extents — either to a new rectangle (`from`/`to`) or to a custom closed L-shape / P-line `polygon` (>= 3 corners) — and atomically syncs the referenced enlarged plan view's crop box and polygonal `cropPolygon` in lockstep (Revit behavior).

```ts
setCalloutBoundary(ctx: ScriptContext, calloutId: string, spec: CalloutBoundarySpec): void
```

Topics: callout, enlarged plan, crop, crop polygon, p-line, l-shape, boundary

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
    const { calloutId } = documents.enlargedPlan(ctx, { parent: plan, name: "Enlarged Core", from: { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, to: { x: units.ft(12), y: units.ft(10) }, scale: 24 });
    documents.setCalloutBoundary(ctx, calloutId, {
      polygon: [
        { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) },
        { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) },
        { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(5) },
        { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(5) },
        { x: units.ft(10), y: units.ft(10) },
        { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(10) },
      ],
    });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.place

Puts a view (a plan, a schedule, a detail) on a sheet at a point (its centre, from the sheet's lower-left corner), with optional scale and viewport title/north-arrow offsets; returns the viewport's id.

```ts
place(ctx: ScriptContext, sheetId: string, viewId: string, at: SheetPoint, scale?: number, title?: { offset?: { x: Measure; y: Measure }; ruleLength?: Measure; northArrowOffset?: { x: Measure; y: Measure } }): string
```

## documents.editSchedule

Edits a list schedule view in one undo step: add, move, remove or rename columns, filter, sort, group, totals (an equipment schedule's sort, a fixture schedule's DFU total). The same steps the grid's Columns menu and the agent's bim_schedule_define send; a form schedule (panel slots) refuses.


## documents.schedule

A schedule view; returns its id. Give classes (rooms, spaces, zones, equipment, any class documents.scheduleFields lists) with field paths or full columns, filters, sort, groups and totals; or a category for a one-category list. Put it on a sheet with documents.place; change it later with documents.editSchedule.

```ts
schedule(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; category: ScheduleCategory; columns: readonly string[]; title?: string; id?: string } | { name: string; classes: readonly string[]; columns: readonly (string | ScheduleColumn)[]; levels?: readonly string[]; filters?: readonly ScheduleFilter[]; sort?: readonly (string | { path: string; direction: "asc" | "desc" })[]; groups?: readonly (string | { path: string; header?: boolean; footer?: boolean; totals?: boolean })[]; totals?: boolean; includeSubclasses?: boolean; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: schedule, make a schedule, room schedule, space schedule, equipment schedule, table, classes

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const rooms = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Room schedule", classes: ["arch.room"], columns: ["number", "name", "area"], sort: ["number"], totals: true });
    const equipmentSchedule = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Equipment schedule", category: "mechanical_equipment", columns: ["mark", "type_name", "level"] });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "A-601", name: "Schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, rooms, { x: units.mm(150), y: units.mm(400) });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, equipmentSchedule, { x: units.mm(450), y: units.mm(400) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.planLabels

Returns every rendered text label on a plan view (paper mm coordinates and bounding boxes) plus any overlapping pairs, so scripts can verify legibility and move colliding tags.

```ts
planLabels(ctx: ScriptContext, viewRef: string): { viewId: string; scale: number; labels: { text: string; at: { xMm: number; yMm: number }; sizeMm: number; anchor: string; box: { minX: number; minY: number; maxX: number; maxY: number } }[]; overlaps: { a: string; b: string; overlapAreaMm2: number }[] }
```

Topics: plan labels, overlaps, legibility, tags, inspect, qa

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const walls = building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(30), y: units.ft(20) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(20) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(8), height: units.ft(10) });
    const plan = documents.planView(ctx, { level: "L1", name: "Level 1 - Plan", scale: 48 });
```

## documents.scheduleRows

A schedule's rows as numbers and words, on the model as the script has it so far: cells by column id (quantities in SI), grand totals, the row count. Form schedules (panels, feeders) are add-on reads (electrical.loads).

```ts
scheduleRows(ctx: ScriptContext, schedule: string, window?: { offset?: number; limit?: number }): ScheduleRows
```

Topics: schedule rows, read a schedule, totals, room areas, schedule values

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }], closed: true, thickness: units.in(6), height: units.ft(9) });
    building.walls(ctx, { level: "L1", points: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }], thickness: units.in(4), height: units.ft(9) });
    const bedroom = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "101", name: "Bedroom", outline: [{ x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(0), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const living = building.room(ctx, { level: "L1", number: "102", name: "Living room", outline: [{ x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(0) }, { x: units.ft(32), y: units.ft(14) }, { x: units.ft(14), y: units.ft(14) }] });
    const rooms = documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Room schedule", classes: ["arch.room"], columns: ["number", "name", "area"], sort: ["number"], totals: true });
    const read = documents.scheduleRows(ctx, rooms);
    const m2 = read.rows.reduce((sum, r) => sum + Number(r.cells.area ?? 0), 0);
    ctx.label(`${read.totalRows} rooms, ${Math.round(m2 * 10.7639)} sq ft`);
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.scheduleFields

What a schedule can list and show: every class (no argument), or each named class's fields (path, label, type, unit, how it totals) and relationships for aggregate columns.

```ts
scheduleFields(ctx: ScriptContext, classes?: readonly string[]): readonly ScheduleClassFields[]
```

Topics: schedule fields, schedule classes, what can a schedule show, columns

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const space = documents.scheduleFields(ctx, ["gen.space"])[0];
    const fields = (space?.fields ?? []).filter((f) => f.path === "area" || f.path === "occupants").map((f) => f.path);
    documents.schedule(ctx, { name: "Space schedule", classes: ["gen.space"], columns: ["number", "name", ...fields], totals: true });
  },
});
```

## documents.packSheet

Arranges a sheet's viewports in its drawing area (the editor's Arrange): packed or a grid, optionally shrinking views to a standard scale that fits, as one edit. Returns how many moved.

```ts
packSheet(ctx: ScriptContext, sheet: string, spec?: { mode?: "pack" | "grid"; columns?: number; fitScales?: boolean; minScale?: number; order?: readonly string[]; gap?: Measure }): { moved: number }
```

Topics: sheet layout, arrange sheet, pack views, sheet packing, fit views

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "M-101", name: "Plans" });
    for (const level of ctx.model.levels()) {
      const view = documents.planView(ctx, { level: level.id, name: `${String(level.name)} - Mechanical`, scale: 48 });
      documents.place(ctx, sheet, view, { x: units.mm(100), y: units.mm(100) });
    }
    documents.packSheet(ctx, sheet, { fitScales: true });
  },
});
```

Creates a live diagram view derived from the model by any active pack (`"one_line"`, `"electrical_riser"`, `"controls_diagram"`, `"air_schematic"`, `"plumbing_riser"`, `"plumbing_isometric"`, …; `documents.diagramKinds(ctx)` lists all available kinds). For `one_line`, pass `hints: { faultCurrent: true, lengthMode: "shortest" | "manhattan" | "explicit", showLoads: true, minLoadRatingA: 60, phaseScope: "all" | "new" | "existing" | "demolition" }` to annotate live 3D-estimated feeder lengths, available fault current (AFC vs kAIC), filter branch loads by breaker size, or generate new-work vs demolition single-lines. Returns the view id.

```ts
diagram(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { name: string; kind: string; hints?: DiagramHints; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: diagram, live diagram, controls diagram, lighting controls diagram, one-line, fault current, afc, feeder length, riser, isometric, air schematic

```ts
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
```

```ts
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const library = documents.detailLibrary(ctx);
    ctx.label(`${library.components.length} detail components`);
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

## documents.formKinds

The form schedule kinds the model's add-ons offer (panel, switchboard, feeder, connection_types, equipment_connections, lighting_controls…) and whether each is the schedule of one element.

```ts
formKinds(ctx: ScriptContext): readonly { kind: string; boundToElement: boolean }[]
```

Topics: form schedule, panel schedule, switchboard schedule, feeder schedule, lighting controls schedule

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    ctx.label(documents.formKinds(ctx).map((f) => f.kind).join(", "));
    ctx.edit({ type: "create_level", levelId: ctx.id("level"), name: "Roof", elevationMm: 9000 });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.formSchedule

A form schedule view (panel, switchboard, feeder, lighting_controls…) with the add-on's built-in form, filled live from the model; rules (a load read's rules.id) prints code demand factors. Returns its id; put it on a sheet with documents.place.

```ts
formSchedule(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: { kind: string; name: string; element?: string; rules?: string; id?: string }): string
```

Topics: panel schedule, form schedule, switchboard schedule, lighting controls schedule, controls schedule, schedule a panel

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true, kinds: ["part"] },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    equipment.place(ctx, { level: "L1", type: "builtin:panelboard-125-208-1ph@1", at: { x: units.ft(1), y: units.ft(13) }, mark: "LP-1" });
    const panel = ctx.model.ofKind("part").find((p) => p.mark === "LP-1");
    if (!panel) throw new Error("No LP-1");
    const loads = ctx.read<{ rules: { id: string } }>("electrical.loads", { panel: "LP-1", nec_edition: "2023" });
    const schedule = documents.formSchedule(ctx, { kind: "panel", name: "Panel LP-1 schedule", element: panel.id, rules: loads.rules.id });
    const controls = documents.formSchedule(ctx, { kind: "lighting_controls", name: "Lighting controls schedule" });
    const sheet = documents.sheet(ctx, { number: "E-601", name: "Panel & control schedules" });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, schedule, { x: units.mm(250), y: units.mm(350) });
    documents.place(ctx, sheet, controls, { x: units.mm(620), y: units.mm(350) });
  },
});
```

</details>

## documents.detailView

Creates a 2D CAD drafting detail view (default scale 16 = 3/4" = 1'-0"). Alias for `drafting.view`. Returns the view's id.

```ts
detailView(ctx: ScriptContext, spec: DetailViewSpec): string
```

Topics: detail view, drafting view, mechanical detail, 2d detail, section detail

<details><summary>Example script</summary>

```ts
import { defineScript, units, routes, parts, building, equipment, documents, markups, drafting, checks, electrical } from "@permitzip/bim-script";
export default defineScript({
  kind: "layout",
  reads: { levels: true },
  parameters: {},
  run(ctx) {
    const detail = documents.detailView(ctx, { name: "M-501 Mechanical Details", scale: 16, discipline: "mechanical" });
    drafting.rect(ctx, { view: detail, at: { x: units.in(0), y: units.in(0) }, width: units.in(36), height: units.in(18), lineStyle: "wide" });
    drafting.fitCrop(ctx, detail);
  },
});
```

</details>
